title: Battle of Uhud
summary: The Battle of Uhud was fought near Mount Uhud, north of Medina, between the early Muslims and the Quraysh of Mecca, who were led by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and sought revenge for Badr. Muslim archers left their hill posts, the Meccan cavalry struck from behind, and the Muslims suffered heavy losses.

uncertainty.note: Year 625 is given by both sources; the day is not settled (Wikipedia GA gives 23 March 625, 7 Shawwal 3 AH).

when.display: 23 March 625 (day per Wikipedia; year only per Britannica)

where.modern_name: Mount Uhud, north of Medina, Saudi Arabia
where.historical_name: Valley near Mount Uhud, north of Medina, Hejaz (Arabia)

importance.justification: Second major clash between Muhammad's community and Mecca, a Muslim setback that preceded the Battle of the Trench.

audience_note: Describes battle deaths and, per tradition, mutilation of corpses.
